objectives: To inculcate critical reasoning and system thinking to take decisions.

To understand Critical reasoning, examine assumptions, uncover hidden values, evaluate
evidence, accomplish actions, and assess conclusions.

To learn a holistic approach to analysis that focuses on the way a system’s constituent parts
interrelated and how systems work overtime and within the context of larger systems

To formulate solutions for social and business enterprises using critical thinking and
brainstorming and covert opportunities into innovation products and services.

outcomes.description: Apply critical reasoning so as to have clarity and wisdom while decision making.

Apply systems thinking concepts to enhance individual and collaborative skills to
recognize opportunities and find innovative solutions for the same.

Apply and analyse systems thinking, critical thinking, lateral thinking, creative thinking
to different real-life scenarios.

Understand how to translate broadly defined opportunities into innovation products and
services and create a business or social enterprise.

crst.description:
This is a perspective course which exposes students to the disciplines of building and
evaluating rational arguments and using a system perspective in applied engineering.
Critical reasoning and system thinking enhances the though process with reasoning and
critical analysis to take to the final decision in order to solve any specific problems. It
enables seeing and understanding systems as wholes rather than as collections of parts, as a web of
interconnections that work together to deliver an outcome.
textBooks: Concise Guide to Critical Thinking by Lewis Vaughn
Critical Thinking by Tom Chatfield
Managing Complex Systems - Thinking Outside the Box by Howard Eisner A

Critical Thinking Tools for Taking Charge of Your Professional and Personal Life
By Richard Paul, Linda Elder · 2020
referenceBooks: Thinking Fast and Slow by Daniel Kahneman
Strategies for creative problem solving by H Scott Fogler and Steven E LeBlanc
Critical Thinking A Concise Guide By Tracy Bowell, Gary Kemp · 2002

topics:
Introduction, foundations and principles of critical reasoning, concepts in critical
reasoning, analyzing reasoning, evaluating reasoning, Integrated reasoning, uncritical and
critical reasoning, scientific reasoning, strategic reasoning, analytical reasoning, different

arguments, valid & invalid arguments, sound & unsound arguments, inductive and
deductive arguments, descriptions, explanations, clarifications, illustrations and summary.

brainstorming, fish bone analysis, thinking out of the box, lateral thinking tools &
techniques, Information and data gathering and analysis, evaluating & prioritizing ideas, six
thinking hats method, problem solving in teams, planning in teams, Tools and applications

advanced subjects like Computer Organization and Architecture, Microprocessor through
Interfacing, VLSI Designing.

numbers, complements, signed binary numbers, binary codes, error detection and error
correction codes. Boolean Algebra and Logic Gates: Basic definitions, axiomatic definition
of Boolean algebra, basic theorems and properties of Boolean algebra, Boolean functions,
canonical and standard forms, other logic operations, digital logic gates.

Digital systems, binary numbers, number base conversions, octal and hexadecimal

correction codes. Boolean Algebra and Logic Gates: Basic definitions, axiomatic definition
of Boolean algebra, basic theorems and properties of Boolean algebra, Boolean functions,
canonical and standard forms, other logic operations, digital logic gates.

Essential and Nonessential
prime Implicants.

Essential and Nonessential

Memories such as ROM, RAM, EPROM.

Binary Multiplier, Magnitude Comparator, Decoders, Encoders, Multiplexers, and
Demultiplexers.
Memories such as ROM, RAM, EPROM.

states, ring counter, Johnson counter. Random access memory, memory decoding, error
detection and correction, read only memory, programmable logic array, programmable
array logic, sequential programmable devices. A/D and D/A converters.

ds.description:
This subject gives an overview of data structure concepts including arrays, stack, queues,
linked lists, trees, and graphs. Discussions shall be held of various implementations of these
data structures in real life. This subject also examines algorithms for sorting and searching.
The concepts of trees and graph-based algorithms shall be introduced.

Sorenson (McGraw Hill).

(Fourth Impression).

Gilberg, R. F., & Forouzan, B. A., Data structures: A pseudocode approach with C++.
Brooks/Cole Publishing, 2001.

objectives:
To expand the holistic perspective based on self-exploration about themselves (human
beings), family, society, and nature/existence and to appreciate the essential
complementarily between ‘VALUES’ and ‘SKILLS’ to ensure sustained happiness and
the real meaning of prosperity which are the core aspirations of all human beings.

To understand the harmony in the human being at all four levels- Individual, family,
society, and nature/existence.
To strengthen the power of self-reflection with the right understanding.

To develop the right evaluation in terms of actions, reactions, and commitments towards
the human goal i.e. mutual happiness and mutual prosperity.

outcomes.description:
Understand and become more aware of self (individual) and our surroundings (family,
society, and nature).

Become more responsible in life for handling problems with sustainable solutions while
keeping human relationships and human nature in mind.
Enhance critical ability for self-reflection.

Boost sensitivity to our commitment in terms of human values, human relationships, and
human society.

objectives: To inculcate critical reasoning and system thinking to take decisions.

To understand Critical reasoning, examine assumptions, uncover hidden values, evaluate
evidence, accomplish actions, and assess conclusions.

To learn a holistic approach to analysis that focuses on the way a system’s constituent parts
interrelated and how systems work overtime and within the context of larger systems

To formulate solutions for social and business enterprises using critical thinking and
brainstorming and covert opportunities into innovation products and services.

outcomes.description: Apply critical reasoning so as to have clarity and wisdom while decision making.

Apply systems thinking concepts to enhance individual and collaborative skills to
recognize opportunities and find innovative solutions for the same.

Apply and analyse systems thinking, critical thinking, lateral thinking, creative thinking
to different real-life scenarios.

Understand how to translate broadly defined opportunities into innovation products and
services and create a business or social enterprise.

crst.description:
This is a perspective course which exposes students to the disciplines of building and
evaluating rational arguments and using a system perspective in applied engineering.
Critical reasoning and system thinking enhances the though process with reasoning and
critical analysis to take to the final decision in order to solve any specific problems. It
enables seeing and understanding systems as wholes rather than as collections of parts, as a web of
interconnections that work together to deliver an outcome.
textBooks: Concise Guide to Critical Thinking by Lewis Vaughn
Critical Thinking by Tom Chatfield
Managing Complex Systems - Thinking Outside the Box by Howard Eisner A

Critical Thinking Tools for Taking Charge of Your Professional and Personal Life
By Richard Paul, Linda Elder · 2020
referenceBooks: Thinking Fast and Slow by Daniel Kahneman
Strategies for creative problem solving by H Scott Fogler and Steven E LeBlanc
Critical Thinking A Concise Guide By Tracy Bowell, Gary Kemp · 2002

advanced subjects like Computer Organization and Architecture, Microprocessor through
Interfacing, VLSI Designing.

correction codes. Boolean Algebra and Logic Gates: Basic definitions, axiomatic definition
of Boolean algebra, basic theorems and properties of Boolean algebra, Boolean functions,

evidence, accomplish actions, and assess conclusions.

interrelated and how systems work overtime and within the context of larger systems

interconnections that work together to deliver an outcome.

interconnections that work together to deliver an outcome.
